title: GROUP BY: bundling rows into piles

steps.title: Piles by category
steps.task: Fill the blank with the column we group the piles by.
hints: Each category has an id number.
steps.expected_sql: SELECT category_id, count(*) FROM products GROUP BY category_id;
steps.seed_sql: SELECT category_id, count(*) FROM products GROUP BY ___;
steps.memory_trick: GROUP BY = 'make a pile for each…'

steps.title: Run the piles
steps.prompt: Type the pile query for real. The Output pane shows one row per category, with its count.
steps.task: Try typing: SELECT category_id, count(*) FROM products GROUP BY category_id;
hints: Type: SELECT category_id, count(*) FROM products GROUP BY category_id;
steps.expected_sql: SELECT category_id, count(*) FROM products GROUP BY category_id;

steps.title: Fix the missing GROUP BY
steps.task: Fix it by adding the missing GROUP BY.
hints: The error is about mixing a column with an aggregate.
One pile per category_id makes it legal.
Add a clause after FROM products.
Fix by appending GROUP BY category_id.
steps.expected_sql: SELECT category_id, count(*) FROM products GROUP BY category_id;
steps.memory_trick: Aggregates get lonely: give them a GROUP BY.

steps.title: SUM - money piles
steps.prompt:
COUNT counts; SUM adds. 'What is each category worth?'
SUM(price) adds all the prices in each pile.
steps.task: Try typing: SELECT category_id, sum(price) FROM products GROUP BY category_id;
hints: Type: SELECT category_id, sum(price) FROM products GROUP BY category_id;
steps.expected_sql: SELECT category_id, sum(price) FROM products GROUP BY category_id;
steps.memory_trick: sum(price) = 'add up the prices in each pile'.

steps.title: Predict the biggest pile
steps.task: Which category has the most products?
hints: The names come from the categories table.
It's where ras el hanout and saffron live.
steps.memory_trick: Read piles like a top-ten chart.
